money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The official currency is the Trinidad and Tobago Dollar (TTD). You can exchange some foreign currencies but not AUD for TTD at commercial banks and official exchange bureaus. Most international hotels and tourist facilities accept credit and debit cards. ATMs are widely available across the country. Criminals target ATMs, so take care when using one. Ask your bank whether your ATM card will work in Trinidad and Tobago.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. They can include lengthy prison sentences in local jails, even for a small quantity of illegal drugs. Research the local laws before you travel.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Sodomy is a criminal offence punishable with a prison term of up to 5 years. There are laws prohibiting LGBTQIA+ individuals from entering the country, but in practice these laws are rarely enforced. Serious crimes, including murder and treason, can attract the death penalty. Other illegal activities include: public nudity in non-designated areas indecent language, such as swearing wearing army or police camouflage clothing as a civilian Carrying ammunition when arriving, leaving or travelling through Trinidad and Tobago is also illegal. laws.rule: If you plan to bring medication, check if it's legal with the Trinidad and Tobago Ministry of Health - Chemistry Food and Drug Division.

laws.rule: To drive in Trinidad and Tobago, you need both: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital drivers licences may not be accepted) a valid International Driving Permit (IDP) You must get your IDP before leaving Australia.
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: All foreign operators must meet the Civil Aviation Authority before any recreational or commercial drone operation. Registration is mandatory for a drone of 750 g or more flying at 40 m/s or more, and involves a webinar and a form. Flights outside the UAS Regulations, and commercial flights, need TTCAA approval, with a letter of indemnity and proof of insurance. A No Fly Zones webmap is published.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Military or camouflage clothing of any kind is illegal; it is reserved for the armed forces. Public nudity is prohibited. Evening dining is usually elegantly casual and most places have a dress code. Licensed taxis have number plates beginning with H; use an official tour guide.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: TTCAA registers drones and approves commercial operations; all foreign operators must meet TTCAA before any recreational or commercial flying. No public operator register was found.

items.text: No public list of approved drone operators was found on the TTCAA UAS page.

Any flight that breaks the UAS Regulations or counts as commercial needs TTCAA approval, with a letter giving coordinates, time, duration and altitude, a letter of indemnity and proof of insurance, plus approval from other agencies where needed. Registration is mandatory for a drone of 750 g or more and 40 m/s or faster, and optional below that. Pilot-licence levels were not read.

TTCAA states that all foreign operators are required to meet with it before any recreational or commercial operations in Trinidad and Tobago. Registration involves a virtual webinar and a fillable form (drones@caa.gov.tt).
TTCAA publishes a No Fly Zones webmap to check before flying.
